messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

First, filter eligible_events by received_time <= 100.

Then, for each event_id, choose the highest visible revision for each event_id. That means for each event ID, there might be multiple revisions (with same event_id? Actually each event_id seems unique; revision numbers are per report. The note says "choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id". So each event_id may have multiple revisions (same event_id but different revision values). So we need to group by event_id, and among those with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff, select the one with highest revision number. That will be the visible report for that event. If there are revisions beyond cutoff, they are not considered.

After that, keep chosen events whose event_time <= target_time (100). These events are historical events up to target_time that are visible at the cutoff.

We apply these events in order of (event_time, event_id) (lexicographically by event_time first, then event_id) starting from initial_stock =12. We simulate receipts: add quantity to stock. Demands: consume min(stock, quantity). If quantity > stock, we sell all stock, subtract stock to zero, and the unmet quantity is lost (lost sales). We count lost quantity for historical lost.

After processing events up to target_time, we record stock_at_target (stock after all processed historical events), and also total historical_lost through target_time.

Now, after reconstruction, we apply future_schedule events (times 101 to 118) in (event_time, event_id) order. Starting from the reconstructed stock_at_target as the stock at time 100.

We simulate receipts/demands similar. Compute final stock at horizon_time = 130 after applying all future events ≤ horizon_time? Actually horizon_time is 130, but future schedule only goes to 118; still we consider up to horizon_time; there may be no events beyond. So after applying all future events (time <= horizon_time), we have stock_at_horizon.

Compute future_lost: lost quantity from future events only (not including historical lost). Also, find the first future stockout time: earliest event_time among future events where demand quantity > stock before the demand (i.e., unmet demand > 0). If no future demand yields unmet demand (i.e., all demands satisfied fully), then return -1.

Edge Cases: some historical events have quantity 0 - they have no effect. Some events have quantity > 0. We will have to process all with zero values too but they have no effect.

4) Sort selected events by (event_time, event_id). Since event_time may have ties? Possibly, but we will sort by event_time, then string ordering of event_id.

5) Simulate.

6) Report stock_at_target and historical_lost.

7) Apply future_schedule events sorted by (event_time, event_id). Compute final stock, future_lost, first_future_stockout_time.
